text:
jia: Heads-up — saw a measurable quality dip on mixed zh+ko testset after we onboarded butterfly-lite-q5a. ~6 BLEU drop vs fp16 baseline on the same eval split. anyone seen this pattern before?
sofia: ouch. is this on the full test split or a focused subset?
jia: focused subset: 2k mixed-script news headlines (han + jamo/compat jamo). overall BLEU -6.1, chrF -4.2. errors look tokenization-y, examples below.
jia: example input: 
```
한국어와中文이섞인제목 테스트
```
jia: fp16 decode (detok): "한국어와 中文이 섞인 제목 테스트"
jia: q5a decode (detok): "한국어 와中 文이섞 인제 목 테스트"
miguel: wow that spacing looks like subtoken boundary shifts. could be UTF normalization or tokenizer preproc change. did we switch a tokenizer build or add a pre-token normalizer in the bring-up?
priya: butterfly-lite onboarding changed token-merge rules to be slightly more aggressive for CJK to reduce vocab size — but that shouldn't introduce interleaved spaces inside han clusters. sounds like a detokenizer mismatch downstream.
anya: quick repro on CPU: 
```
# run tokenizer on sample
python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.from_file('models/butterfly-lite-q5a/tokenizer.json'); print(t.encode('한국어와中文이섞인제목 테스트').tokens)"
```
anya: output tokens: ['▁한국', '어', '와', '中', '文', '이', '섞', '인', '제', '목', '테', '스트']
anya: fp16 tokenizer tokens (baseline): ['▁한국', '어', '와', '中文', '이', '섞', '인', '제목', '테스트']
sofia: interesting — baseline merges 中文 and 제목 but q5a splits them. merging differences will shift token ids and likely detok glue rules. q5a’s BPE merges seem to have lost multi-char han merges.
miguel: confirm whether tokenizer.json came from the same vocabulary/artifact. sometimes onboarding scripts regenerate vocab with different merge ordering. check model metadata:
```
cat models/butterfly-lite-q5a/metadata.json
```
priya: metadata shows vocab_hash mismatch with fp16 baseline — yes looks like we accidentally used an older tokenizer build when packaging quantized weights.
ja: that explains it. but why did BLEU drop so much? small tokenization diffs can cascade under n-gram metrics. also mixedscript cases are particularly sensitive.
anya: ran sacrebleu quick compare on the focused subset:
```
fp16: BLEU 28.7
q5a: 22.6
```
anya: sample diff shows misaligned n-grams due to extra spaces after detok for CJK-run boundaries.
sofia: for immediate mitigation we can add a post-detok normalization hook that collapses stray spaces between Han and adjacent scripts, e.g. regex to remove spaces between Han<->Jamo/Latin clusters. not ideal long-term but buys time.
miguel: agreed. long term: repackage q5a with the canonical tokenizer.json from fp16 run or regenerate merges keeping multi-char han merges preferred. also add a unit test: mixedscript roundtrip tokenization -> detokenization must be idempotent for 99% of samples.
priya: opened a ticket in triage and added bisect label. assigning to @eng-ml-tokenizer to find where tokenizer.json diverged during build pipeline.
ops-bot: CI run queued: https://ci.internal/redwood/eng-ml/3912345678/tokenizer-bisect (logs will appear in the ticket).
ja: quick patch applied to staging detok to collapse han-adjacent spaces, pushed patch id 8f3a. staging re-eval sending now.
anya: staging re-eval looks promising: BLEU up to 26.9 (still below fp16 but big improvement).
sofia: good triage path. can we add a smoke test in the onboarding workflow that compares tokenization profiles (merge counts, top merges) between baseline and quantized build and fails if >X% divergence?
miguel: yes — compute merge overlap Jaccard on top 500 merges + a small mixed-script BLEU sanity check. i'll prototype today.
priya: thanks everyone. leaving this thread here — will update ticket with bisect outcome. :thumbsup:
jia: thanks team :heart:
